titulo: AI readiness rubric and its caveats
lead: An AI readiness score helps you find what's broken, as long as you know how it's calculated. No score is official: each scanner picks its own criteria and weights. Here you compare two open INEMA rubrics, read what weighs most, and learn what the score does not prove.
objetivo: run an AI readiness score, read the criteria that weigh most, and know what the score does not prove.

aprende.t: How WebMCP Readiness and agente-ready calculate the score
The criteria that weigh most: bot access, content, entity
The caveats: WebMCP weight, questions and answers, small sample
Fix what weighs most and run it again

hero_alt: Inspector with a clipboard checks the entrance of a commercial building, with a ramp and a glass door.

nos.detalhe: Both scanners read what the server delivers: robots.txt, sitemap, the home page, and a few pages. The agente-ready reads like a bot that doesn't run JavaScript.

Each criterion has a weight. In agente-ready (v1.0.0, 10/19/2026) the weights are public in a file: bot access 30, extractable content 26, discovery 18, entity 14, WebMCP 8, forms 4. llms.txt weighs only 2.
Points earned over the weights that apply to the site. A criterion that doesn't apply (a site with no forms, no languages) is left out of the calculation instead of counting as a failure.
The list of failures sorted by weight is the plan: a search bot blocked at the CDN (12) is worth more than llms.txt (2).

nos.sub: what the score does not prove
nos.detalhe: A high score is not a citation. The weights are the choice of whoever made the rubric, and the sample is a few pages. Use it to find defects, never as a promise to the client.

secoes.legenda: The score helps you prioritize fixes. Citations are measured in lessons 2 and 3.

secoes.titulo: The two rubrics and the caveats

texto: The INEMA scanner adds up four blocks: WebMCP 30%, SEO 30%, GEO 20%, and AEO 20%. Each finding is worth pass, warning, or fail; an informational-only finding is worth 0.7.
GEO looks at entity, substantial content (250+ words), authorship and date, sources, and semantic HTML. AEO looks at questions in headings, direct answers, lists, and tables.
In Readiness, a site without WebMCP gets a low overall score even with perfect SEO, because that block weighs 30%. WebMCP is a draft with no stable browser (lesson 7): read that block as preparation.

AEO criteria reward headings phrased as questions with a short answer right after. That is clarity for the reader, not an AI technique with a source behind it. And the FAQ rich result stopped showing in Google on 05/07/2026: FAQPage markup no longer gets you a showcase.
Don't create artificial questions just to score points.
Open evolution of Readiness: weights in a versioned file, with the reason and source for each criterion; WebMCP weighs 8 out of 100; llms.txt weighs 2.
Limits: sample of home + 4 pages, CDN test by User-Agent only, WebMCP detected only in static code.

secoes.titulo: Run it and read the score
secoes.sub: agente-ready only reads public pages, with no API (detailed in course 7). WebMCP Readiness (webmcp.inema.pro) opens the page in a disposable browser and goes deeper only on the URL you provide.

blocos.conteudo:
git clone https://github.com/inematds/inemaseo-sistemas && cd inemaseo-sistemas/ferramentas/agente-ready
python3 agente-ready.py https://seusite.com --saida saida/seusite
# output: relatorio.html, agente-ready.json and criterios.csv
# the weights live in pesos.json: disagree, change them and run again

# AI readiness — <seusite.com>
| date | tool and version | score | 3 heaviest failures | fixed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dd/mm/yyyy | agente-ready 1.0.0 | <n> | <failure 1 (weight)>, <failure 2>, <failure 3> | <which> |

abas.html:
agente-ready 1.0.0 on INEMA sites, home + 4 pages:

site                         nota  entidade  conteudo  descoberta  webmcp
inema.club                   93    86        81        100         100
news.inema.pro               72    0         71        100         29
eventos.inema.pro            69    0         62        100         29
guia REA (github.io)         54    0         62        17          29

• inema.club: loses points only for the About/Contact link on the home page and for partial authorship and date.
  • news and eventos: entity scores zero (no Organization/Person with @id on the home page); this is the heaviest fix.
  • guia REA: no sitemap, no lastmod and no canonical; discovery drops to 17.
  • Bot access: 100 on all four.

abas.rot: What the score doesn't tell you
abas.html: None of these scores tells you whether the site is cited. inema.club at 93 and the July measurement of 0 out of 52 neutral citations coexist: readiness is a condition, citation is a result.

secoes.sub: It can be your own site or a client's who gave permission.

exercicios.texto: Run agente-ready (or WebMCP Readiness) on the site and write down the score, the tool with its version, and the 3 heaviest failures.
exercicios.pronto: notas.md has the row with date, tool and version, score, and the 3 failures with the weight of each.

exercicios.texto: Fix the heaviest failure within your reach (for example, the entity on the home page), publish, and run it again.
exercicios.pronto: notas.md has the second row with the new score and the fixed criterion marked as ok.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The site has flawless SEO and a low overall score in WebMCP Readiness. What is the likely explanation?
opcoes: The WebMCP block weighs 30% of the score and the site has no WebMCP.
perguntas.explica: This is the main caveat of this rubric. Read the WebMCP block as preparation, not as an SEO flaw.

perguntas.p: In agente-ready, which fix comes first?
opcoes: Allow AI search bots through the CDN (weight 12).
Add more questions to the headings.
perguntas.explica: The order follows the weight. A blocked search bot takes the site out of the answers; llms.txt is optional.

perguntas.p: inema.club scores 93. What does that prove about citation in the AIs?
opcoes: That it is cited in 93% of answers.
Nothing: readiness is a condition; citation is measured in the dashboards and in the question battery.
That ChatGPT reads the site every day.
perguntas.explica: A rubric score doesn't measure AI answers. That's why lessons 2 and 3 exist.

perguntas.p: The rubric rewards headings written as questions. How do you use that?
opcoes: Turn every heading into a question.
Use a question when it's a real doubt your audience has, for clarity, without creating questions just to score points.
Mark up everything with FAQPage to get a showcase.
perguntas.explica: A real question with a direct answer helps the reader. And the FAQ rich result ended on 05/07/2026.

itens.texto: Each scanner picks its own criteria and weights; prefer public weights.
Bot access, content in the HTML, and entity come before details.
A high score is not a citation. WebMCP and questions in headings are preparation and clarity, not a ranking factor.
